correctness.rationale: The radial function follows from the two-disk inequalities. Ellipse containment is an exact nonnegative algebraic identity with a complete equality set; the parallelogram area is bounded by a determinant in its image. Near each of two isolated maxima the loss is a^2 b alpha^2+2ac|delta|+lower-order terms, and an explicit area-8/3 mixed-parabolic rescaling gives the 8/(3pi^2 a^2 c sqrt(b)) constant. At c=0 a uniform angle difference gives the exact inverse-cosine CDF. For c/epsilon finite, a uniform radial expansion, compact localization and dominated convergence give the stated one-dimensional crossover G, and endpoint integration gives its large-parameter coefficient. Conditional marks are uniform on the same tangent region. All critical expansions were independently numerically checked by the supplied 66052-test standard-library script; numerical tests alone are not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The area of an inscribed centrally symmetric parallelogram is a canonical basic convex-approximation statistic of a symmetric lens; uniform viewing directions make its rarity interpretable. The theorem exposes a real change from a continuum of disk optimizers to two isolated lens contact configurations, including two different angular deficit scales and a quantitatively matched c~epsilon window. The explicit coefficient, crossover, and conditional geometry are directly informative, rather than an arbitrary sample computation or a restatement of the known ellipse.
